newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish premier launches cabinet reform.
newsitem.headline: Polish premier launches cabinet reform.

text.p: Poland moved closer to a sweeping government reorganisation on Tuesday when Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz appointed temporary heads of ministries to be created under the reform.

Cimoszewicz, who faces a bitter row in the ruling leftist coalition over the share-out of power in the reshuffled cabinet, put lesser-known, uncontroversial politicians in charge of setting up the new ministries.
"These people are to prepare the ministries for operation... and ready their charters," Cimoszewicz told reporters before handing over the nominations.

The acting officials are to step down when the actual ministers are appointed upon a deal between the coalitions' two parties -- the ex-communist Democratic Left Alliance (SLD) and the Polish Peasant Party (PSL).

The two parties' dispute over the appointments turned bitter two weeks ago when the SLD's Cimoszewicz sacked the PSL's Foreign Trade Minister Jacek Buchacz, saying his ministry had mismanaged key state assets.

Analysts say, however, that the coalition should stay together until general elections due late next year because neither party wants to lose power and sees no alternative in forming a majority in parliament.
Cimoszewicz put current deputy interior minister Zbigniew Sobotka, linked to the SLD, in charge of setting up the new Ministry of Interior Affairs and Administration.
PSL parliamentary deputy Andrzej Malinowski is to create the new Economy Ministry, which will embrace the current ministries of industry and foreign trade.

The new Treasury Ministry, which starts work in October as the first cabinet portfolio set up under the reform, will be prepared for operations by current deputy privatisation minister Piotr Czyzewski.
The cabinet reform is designed to streamline decision-making and reduce the central government's role in the economy.
